config.title: Type reducer and dispatch for context store

intro.title: Type reducer and dispatch for context store
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed reducer function and dispatch method for a React context store. You'll learn how to define a reducer that handles state updates based on actions, using TypeScript to ensure type safety. The core concepts involve using TypeScript interfaces for actions and state, and implementing a dispatch function to trigger state changes. By the end, you'll have a fully typed context store setup that manages state predictably and prevents common runtime errors.
intro.usecase: In real applications like e-commerce dashboards, you need to manage complex state such as user carts, product filters, and order histories. This pattern allows you to centralize state updates for features like adding items to cart, applying price filters, or updating user preferences. By typing reducers and dispatch, you ensure that state changes are predictable and type-safe across components like product listings, checkout panels, and admin interfaces. This approach prevents bugs in critical user flows and makes the codebase maintainable as the application scales.

objectives: Construct a TypeScript type definition for a reducer function that manages state updates.
Apply TypeScript interfaces or types to define the shape of the state object and action objects.
Initialize a React context provider with typed reducer state and dispatch.
Implement a custom hook that safely provides access to the typed dispatch function from context.
Manipulate state by dispatching typed actions from a component using the custom hook.
Configure a reducer to handle multiple action types with type-safe payloads.
Integrate the typed reducer and dispatch into a functional component to control state flow.

successCriteria: React and createContext are imported from 'react'.

successCriteria: The State interface is defined with a count property of type number.

steps.title: Create initial state object
steps.instruction: Create a constant named 'initialState' that is typed with the State interface and assign it an object with default values.
steps.hint: Use the 'const' keyword to declare a variable named 'initialState' and set it to an object that matches the shape of your State interface.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a typed constant 'initialState' that provides default values matching the State interface.
successCriteria: A constant named 'initialState' is declared with the State type and contains an object with appropriate default values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Define action types
steps.instruction: Define a union type called 'Action' that represents possible action types for your reducer. Include two string literal types: 'INCREMENT' and 'DECREMENT'.
steps.hint: Use the 'type' keyword to create a union type with the pipe (|) operator between the string literals.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of a union type for actions
type Action = 'ADD_TODO' | 'REMOVE_TODO';
steps.expectedOutcome: A union type named 'Action' with 'INCREMENT' and 'DECREMENT' as possible values is created.
successCriteria: The 'Action' type is defined as a union of 'INCREMENT' and 'DECREMENT' string literals.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your Action type includes both 'INCREMENT' and 'DECREMENT' as string literal types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Action type should be a union of 'INCREMENT' and 'DECREMENT' string literals.

steps.title: Define action interface
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface named 'Action' that describes the shape of action objects. It should have a 'type' property of type 'ActionType' and an optional 'payload' property of type 'any'.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and define the required properties with their types.
steps.expectedOutcome: An Action interface is created with the correct property definitions, enabling type-safe action objects in your reducer.
successCriteria: The Action interface is defined with a required 'type' property of type 'ActionType' and an optional 'payload' property of type 'any'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your interface has both the 'type' property (with type 'ActionType') and the optional 'payload' property (with type 'any').
steps.feedbackWrong: The Action interface isn't correctly defined. Remember to use the 'interface' keyword and specify both properties with their types.

steps.title: Create reducer function
steps.instruction: Create a reducer function named 'reducer' that takes the current state (typed as State) and an action (typed as Action) as parameters, and returns a new State object.
steps.hint: The reducer function should handle different action types using a switch statement or if-else conditions. For now, you can return the current state as the default case.
steps.expectedOutcome: A typed reducer function named 'reducer' is created that accepts State and Action parameters and returns a State object.
successCriteria: The reducer function is defined with proper TypeScript types for parameters and return value, and includes a default case that returns the current state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the reducer function has the correct parameter types (State and Action) and returns a State object. Also include a default case that returns the current state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The reducer function is missing or has incorrect structure. Remember to create a function named 'reducer' that takes State and Action parameters and returns a new State object.

steps.title: Define context interface
steps.instruction: Define an interface named ContextValue that describes the shape of your context value. It should have a state property of type State and a dispatch property of type React.Dispatch<Action>.
steps.hint: Create an interface with two properties: state and dispatch. Use the State type you defined earlier for state, and React.Dispatch<Action> for dispatch.
steps.expectedOutcome: An interface named ContextValue is added, specifying state and dispatch properties with appropriate TypeScript types.
successCriteria: The ContextValue interface is defined with state: State and dispatch: React.Dispatch<Action> properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your ContextValue interface includes both required properties: state of type State and dispatch of type React.Dispatch<Action>.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ContextValue interface is missing or incorrect. It should have two properties: state (type State) and dispatch (type React.Dispatch<Action>).

steps.title: Create context with default value
steps.instruction: Create a React context using the context interface you defined earlier, with an undefined default value. Use the createContext function you imported.
steps.hint: Call createContext with a type parameter matching your context interface and pass undefined as the initial value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A typed React context variable is created with undefined as its default value.
successCriteria: The context is created using createContext with the correct type parameter and undefined as the default value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using createContext with the correct type parameter and undefined as the default value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The context wasn't created correctly. Remember to use createContext with your context interface type and undefined as the default value.

steps.title: Create provider component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named CounterProvider that uses useReducer with the reducer function and initialState, and returns the CounterContext.Provider with the state and dispatch as the value.
steps.hint: Define a component that uses useReducer to manage state, then wrap children with CounterContext.Provider passing the state and dispatch in the value prop.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CounterProvider component is defined that uses useReducer and provides the CounterContext.Provider with state and dispatch.
successCriteria: CounterProvider component is created with useReducer, returns CounterContext.Provider, and passes state and dispatch in the value prop.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your component uses useReducer with the reducer and initialState, and returns CounterContext.Provider with state and dispatch in the value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The provider component isn't set up correctly. Review how to create a component that uses useReducer and provides context.

steps.title: Create custom hook for context
steps.instruction: Create a custom hook named useAppContext that returns the context value with proper typing.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls useContext with your context and returns the typed value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A typed custom hook that safely accesses the context value.
successCriteria: The custom hook useAppContext is defined, calls useContext with the correct context, and returns the typed value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your hook is named useAppContext and returns the context value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The custom hook is missing or incorrect. Create a function named useAppContext that returns the context value.

steps.title: Wire dispatch to buttons
steps.instruction: In your consumer component, add two buttons that dispatch the INCREMENT and DECREMENT actions when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the dispatch function from your custom hook to send actions. Each button should have an onClick handler that calls dispatch with the appropriate action object.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two buttons appear in the consumer component that can dispatch INCREMENT and DECREMENT actions to update the count.
successCriteria: The consumer component contains two buttons with onClick handlers that call dispatch with action objects of type 'INCREMENT' and 'DECREMENT'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some UI elements, but make sure both buttons have proper onClick handlers that dispatch the correct actions.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons are missing or not properly connected to dispatch. Check that each button's onClick calls dispatch with the correct action type.
